# Sample With A High Average But No Single Offender

Every single sentence in this fixture document has been written quite deliberately to sit somewhere in the low twenties for its own word count. Not one of them ever crosses the thirty word cap, and so the per sentence rule can find nothing at all to report. The trouble in this prose only becomes visible when the engine steps back and considers the document as one whole connected piece of writing. A reader here faces sentence after sentence of this same sustained moderate length, with no shorter ones mixed in for relief.

The public plain language standards ask writers to keep the average sentence length across a whole document between fifteen and twenty words. This fixture pushes its own running average above that stated ceiling while still keeping every individual sentence inside the thirty cap. That precise combination is exactly the sustained failure mode which the old maximum only rule could never see or ever report. Any tool that only ever checks single sentences would wave this entire document straight through without one single comment, which is wrong.

The average rule needs to see a reasonable number of sentences before it can judge any document fairly and without excessive noise. Ten counted sentences is the minimum sample size this engine accepts before it will even compute the running average at all. This third paragraph exists mostly to carry the whole fixture safely past that minimum with more sentences of matching sustained length. Its final sentence now closes the fixture while it still holds the same deliberate twenty something word rhythm as all the rest.
